title: Money and Banking
description: Class 11 / ISC Economics: meaning and functions of money, commercial banks and credit creation, and the functions of the central bank (RBI).

topics.title: Meaning and Functions of Money
topics.concept:
Before money, people exchanged goods directly for goods — the barter system. Barter had serious problems: it needed a double coincidence of wants (each person had to want exactly what the other offered), there was no common measure of value, goods could not be stored easily, and there was no way to make deferred (future) payments. Money was invented to solve all these problems.

Money is anything that is generally accepted as a medium of exchange and in payment of debts. Modern money includes coins, currency notes and bank deposits. Money performs four main functions:

  • Medium of exchange — money is accepted in exchange for all goods and services, so we no longer need a double coincidence of wants. (This is the primary function.)
  • Measure (or unit) of value — the value of every good is measured and expressed in money (price), giving a common yardstick.
  • Store of value — money can be saved and stored for future use, because it does not perish.
  • Standard of deferred payments — money allows borrowing and lending, so payments can be made in the future (e.g. paying back a loan).

By performing these functions, money removes the difficulties of barter and makes trade, saving and investment easy — which is why it is one of the most important inventions in economic life.

examples.problem: Example 1: What is the 'double coincidence of wants', and which function of money removes it?
examples.solution:
It was a problem of barter.

  • Each person had to want exactly what the other offered.
  • The medium of exchange function of money removes this difficulty.
examples.answer: It is the barter requirement that each party wants what the other offers; money's medium-of-exchange function removes it.

examples.problem: Example 2: State the four functions of money.
examples.solution:
Recall the list.

  • Medium of exchange, measure of value.
  • Store of value, standard of deferred payments.
examples.answer: Medium of exchange, measure of value, store of value, and standard of deferred payments.

examples.problem: Example 3: Which function lets us save money for future use?
examples.solution:
Money does not perish.

  • The store of value function.

recap:
• Barter problems: double coincidence of wants, no common value measure, no store of value, no deferred payment.
  • Money = anything generally accepted as a medium of exchange (coins, notes, deposits).
  • Four functions: medium of exchange (primary), measure of value, store of value, standard of deferred payments.

quiz.q: The primary function of money is as a:
quiz.explanation: The primary function of money is as a medium of exchange.
Barter needed a double coincidence of wants, which money removes.

topics.title: Commercial Banks and Credit Creation
topics.concept:
A commercial bank is a financial institution that accepts deposits from the public and lends money, in order to earn a profit. Banks are the backbone of the modern money system. Their two primary functions are:

  • Accepting deposits — people keep their money safely in banks. The main kinds are the current account (for businesses, withdraw any time, no interest), the savings account (small savers, some interest), and the fixed (time) deposit (money kept for a fixed period at higher interest).
  • Advancing loans (lending) — banks lend the deposited money to borrowers (as loans, cash credit, overdrafts) and charge interest. The difference between the interest charged on loans and paid on deposits is the bank's profit.

Banks also perform secondary functions — transferring money, issuing cheques and cards, lockers, and so on.

The most remarkable thing banks do is credit creation (money creation). When a bank receives deposits, it keeps only a small fraction as a cash reserve (because not all depositors withdraw at once) and lends out the rest. The borrower spends the money, which comes back to the banking system as a new deposit, part of which is again lent out — and so on. In this way, the banking system as a whole can create deposits (credit) several times the original cash. This is why commercial banks are said to "create money." The amount they can create depends on the reserve ratio — the smaller the fraction kept as reserve, the more credit can be created.

examples.problem: Example 1: What are the two primary functions of a commercial bank?
examples.solution:
Deposits in, loans out.

  • Accepting deposits from the public.
  • Advancing loans (lending money).
examples.answer: Accepting deposits from the public and advancing loans (lending money).

examples.problem: Example 2: How does a bank earn its profit?
examples.solution:
From the interest gap.

  • It charges more interest on loans than it pays on deposits.
  • The difference is its profit.
examples.answer: From the difference between the interest it charges on loans and the interest it pays on deposits.

examples.solution:
They keep a fraction, lend the rest.

  • They keep only a small cash reserve and lend out the rest.
  • The loaned money returns as new deposits and is lent again, multiplying credit.
examples.answer: By keeping only a small reserve and lending the rest; the loans return as new deposits and are re-lent, so the system creates credit many times the original cash.

recap:
• Commercial bank: accepts deposits (current, savings, fixed) and advances loans; profit = interest gap.
  • Credit creation: keep a fraction as reserve, lend the rest; loans return as deposits and are re-lent → banks create money several times the cash.
  • Amount depends on the reserve ratio (lower reserve → more credit).

quiz.q: The two primary functions of a commercial bank are accepting deposits and:
quiz.explanation: Banks accept deposits and advance loans.

quiz.q: Banks can create credit because they keep only a:
options: Small fraction of deposits as reserve
quiz.explanation: Keeping only a fraction as reserve lets banks lend the rest and create credit.

topics.title: The Central Bank
topics.concept:
At the top of a country's banking system is the central bank — the apex institution that controls and supervises the whole monetary and banking system. In India the central bank is the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). Unlike commercial banks, the central bank does not aim at profit; its goal is to manage the economy's money and credit in the public interest. Its main functions are:

  • Bank of issue — the central bank has the sole right to issue currency notes in the country. This keeps the currency uniform and under control.
  • Banker to the government — it keeps the government's accounts, makes its payments and receipts, and advises it on financial matters.
  • Bankers' bank — it acts as the banker to all commercial banks: they keep reserves with it, and it lends to them and supervises them.
  • Lender of last resort — in a crisis, when commercial banks cannot get money elsewhere, the central bank lends to them, preventing the banking system from collapsing.
  • Controller of credit — this is its most important function. The central bank controls the amount of money and credit in the economy (to manage inflation and growth) using tools such as the bank rate (repo rate), cash reserve ratio (CRR) and open market operations (buying/selling government securities).
  • Custodian of foreign exchange reserves.

So while commercial banks deal with the public for profit, the central bank stands above them, managing the nation's money supply, guarding the value of the currency, and keeping the financial system stable. Money, commercial banks and the central bank together make up the heart of the monetary system.

examples.problem: Example 1: What is the central bank of India, and how does it differ from a commercial bank?
examples.solution:
It is the apex, non-profit bank.

  • The Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
  • It controls the whole banking system and does not aim at profit, unlike commercial banks.
examples.answer: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI); unlike commercial banks, it controls the whole monetary system and does not aim at profit.

examples.problem: Example 2: Why is the central bank called the 'lender of last resort'?
examples.solution:
It rescues banks in crisis.

  • When commercial banks cannot get money elsewhere, the central bank lends to them.
  • This prevents the banking system from collapsing.
examples.answer: Because it lends to commercial banks in a crisis when they can get money nowhere else, preventing the system from collapsing.

examples.problem: Example 3: Name two tools the central bank uses to control credit.
examples.solution:
Recall the credit-control tools.

  • The bank rate (repo rate) and the cash reserve ratio (CRR).
  • (Also open market operations.)
examples.answer: The bank rate (repo rate) and the cash reserve ratio (CRR) — also open market operations.

recap:
• Central bank (RBI) = apex, non-profit institution controlling the monetary system.
  • Functions: bank of issue (currency), banker to government, bankers' bank, lender of last resort, controller of credit (bank/repo rate, CRR, open market operations), custodian of forex.

quiz.q: The central bank of India is the:
quiz.explanation: The RBI is India's central bank.

quiz.q: The sole right to issue currency notes belongs to the:
quiz.explanation: The central bank is the bank of issue (issues currency).

questions.q: Direct exchange of goods for goods is the:
questions.explanation: Direct goods-for-goods exchange is barter.

questions.q: A major problem of barter was the lack of a:
questions.explanation: Barter needed a double coincidence of wants.

questions.q: Anything generally accepted as a medium of exchange is:
questions.explanation: That is the definition of money.

questions.q: The primary function of money is as a:
questions.explanation: The medium of exchange is the primary function.

questions.q: Expressing the value of every good in money is the ____ function.
questions.explanation: Money as a common yardstick is the measure of value.

questions.q: Saving money for future use shows the ____ function.
questions.explanation: Money can be stored — the store of value function.

questions.q: A commercial bank's two primary functions are accepting deposits and:
questions.explanation: Banks accept deposits and advance loans.

questions.q: A deposit kept for a fixed period at higher interest is a:
questions.explanation: A fixed/time deposit is kept for a set period at higher interest.

questions.q: A bank's profit comes from the difference between interest on loans and interest on:
questions.explanation: Profit = interest charged on loans − interest paid on deposits.

questions.q: Banks can create credit because they keep only a ____ of deposits as reserve.
questions.explanation: Keeping a small fraction lets them lend the rest and create credit.

questions.q: The apex institution controlling the banking system is the:
questions.explanation: The central bank controls the whole banking system.

questions.q: The central bank of India is the:
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the central bank.

questions.q: The sole right to issue currency notes belongs to the:
questions.explanation: The central bank is the bank of issue.

questions.q: When the central bank lends to banks in a crisis, it acts as the:
questions.explanation: Lending to banks in crisis is the lender-of-last-resort role.

questions.q: Which is a tool the central bank uses to control credit?
questions.explanation: CRR (and the bank rate, open market operations) control credit.

questions.q: A farmer with rice wants cloth, but the weaver wants wheat, not rice. In a barter economy they cannot trade because there is no:
questions.explanation: Barter needs each party to want what the other offers; money solves this as a medium of exchange.

questions.q: If a bank keeps 20% of deposits as reserve and lends the rest, the banking system can create total credit that is ____ the initial cash.
questions.explanation: A low reserve ratio lets re-lending multiply deposits, so total credit is several times the original cash.

questions.q: To fight high inflation, the central bank may raise the repo rate, which tends to make borrowing:
questions.explanation: A higher policy rate raises loan costs, curbing credit and demand to cool inflation.

questions.q: Unlike a commercial bank, the central bank does NOT primarily aim at:
questions.explanation: The central bank works in the public interest, not for profit like commercial banks.

questions.q: During a banking panic, the central bank's role as 'lender of last resort' is vital because it:
options: Prevents the collapse of banks that cannot get funds elsewhere
Prints unlimited notes for the public
questions.explanation: By lending to stressed banks it stops a panic from bringing down the whole system.

questions.q: Money's function as a 'standard of deferred payments' is what makes ____ possible.
options: Borrowing and lending (loans repaid in future)
questions.explanation: Because debts can be expressed and repaid in money over time, credit transactions become workable.

questions.q: A bank reduces its cash reserve ratio. Other things equal, its ability to create credit will:
questions.explanation: A smaller reserve means more of each deposit can be lent, raising credit creation.

questions.q: Keeping the government's accounts and managing its receipts and payments is the central bank acting as:
questions.explanation: Handling government banking business is the 'banker to the government' function.

questions.q: Currency notes in India are uniform and trustworthy largely because they are issued only by the:
questions.explanation: A single issuing authority keeps the currency standard, controlled and credible.

questions.q: Why are money, commercial banks and the central bank studied together?
options: Together they form the monetary and banking system that runs the economy's money
questions.explanation: Money is the medium, commercial banks circulate and create it, and the central bank controls it — one connected system.
